entries.title: Gradius
entries.summary: Konami's NES conversion of its 1985 arcade horizontal shooter: pilot the Vic Viper through alien-infested stages and 'Destroy the core!'
entries.why_it_matters: Konami's first NES release in North America. Its power meter was highly influential, and its cheat code became the Konami Code.
entries.gameplay_notes: One kind of capsule advances a power-up bar at the bottom of the screen; press the button to take the highlighted upgrade. Chip through the walls shielding each boss's core. The NES version simplifies some stage designs and allows two options instead of four.

difficulty.reason: GameSpot called it one of the toughest NES shooters, second only to Contra.

entries.title: The Guardian Legend
entries.summary: Compile's shooter/action-adventure hybrid, published by Broderbund: the Guardian, a transforming 'aerobot' gynoid, triggers the self-destruct devices on Naju, an alien world hurtling toward Earth.
entries.why_it_matters: A classic genre-blend of Zelda-style exploration and 1942-style vertical shooting. It is directed by Compile president Moo Niitani and is a sequel to the MSX game Guardic.

entries.title: Gyromite
entries.summary: Nintendo's R.O.B. robot puzzle platformer, a NES launch title: guide Professor Hector to collect dynamite before time runs out while R.O.B. moves gyros to raise and lower red and blue pillars.
entries.why_it_matters: One of only two Robot Series games. It came in the launch Deluxe Set with R.O.B., the Zapper and Duck Hunt, and R.O.B. was central to how the NES was marketed.
entries.gameplay_notes: Hector can't jump, so he drops onto dynamite. Drop radishes to lure the Smick creatures. R.O.B. places gyros on buttons that press A or B on controller 2; a spinner keeps gyros balanced so both can be held down. Games A and B differ only in how R.O.B. takes commands; Direct mode is for practice.
entries.hltb_note: HLTB NES platform row (4 completions logged; title-matched NES Wikidata item)
entries.collecting_notes: The retail package includes the R.O.B. accessory parts: two claws, two gyros, red and blue trays, a spinner and two storage trays.
entries.content_notes: Needs R.O.B. and the Gyromite accessory kit (claws, gyros, trays, spinner) to play as designed.

entries.title: Laser Invasion
entries.summary: Konami's 1991 multi-genre action game: fly an upgraded AH-64 Apache into enemy territory, land, and infiltrate bases to rescue the captured agent Spider and stop a secret weapon.
entries.why_it_matters: Supports the controller, the NES Zapper and Konami's voice-activated LaserScope headset; the NA manual included a LaserScope rebate.
entries.gameplay_notes: Four missions in three play styles: helicopter flight, on-foot base infiltration with first-person gun segments (Zapper or LaserScope optional), and an all-air third mission. Five continues; lives adjustable in the options.

entries.title: Last Action Hero
entries.summary: Teeny Weeny Games' NES beat 'em up tie-in to the 1993 film Last Action Hero, from Sony Imagesoft.
entries.gameplay_notes: Side-scrolling brawling with no guns or other weapons. The NES version has no car-chase stages and no final Mr. Benedict fight, but adds an exclusive stage based on Danny's version of Hamlet.
entries.hltb_note: HLTB NES platform row (1 completions logged; Wikidata-linked) - low sample
review_flags: The source names Bits Studios as developer of most versions; the census credits Teeny Weeny Games for the NES game.

entries.title: The Last Ninja
entries.summary: Beam Software's NES version of System 3's Last Ninja 2, published by Jaleco: the ninja Armakuni is transported to 20th-century New York to defeat the shogun Kunitoki again.
entries.gameplay_notes: Isometric levels with melee combat, blocking and one-hit-kill shuriken. Find and use items (keys, rope, map) in the right places. Hamburgers give extra lives.
entries.hltb_note: HLTB entry exists but has no NES-specific times (other platforms only); not used.
entries.content_notes: It is Last Ninja 2 under a shortened title, not a port of the first Last Ninja.

entries.title: The Last Starfighter
entries.summary: Mindscape's 1990 NES game, which is Andrew Braybrook's shooter Uridium with a Last Starfighter licence applied: the title, sprites and music changed, but the levels and gameplay are identical.
entries.gameplay_notes: Fly low over the hulls of 15 Super-Dreadnoughts, dodging walls (turn sideways to slip through narrow gaps), fighter waves and indestructible homing mines. Knock out enough defences to trigger 'Land Now!', then land and blow up the ship.

difficulty.reason: Tight wall gaps and mines that can't be destroyed demand precise flying.

entries.hltb_note: HLTB entry exists but has no NES-specific times (other platforms only); not used.
entries.content_notes: Has nothing to do with the film's plot beyond the name.

entries.title: Lee Trevino's Fighting Golf
entries.summary: SNK's 1988 NES version of its arcade golf game, with Lee Trevino as the playable 'Super Mex' (NA version only).
entries.gameplay_notes: Four golfers with different strengths (Super Mex, Pretty Amy, Miracle Chosuke, Big Jumbo) on two courses: a bunker-heavy US course modelled on PGA West Stadium, and a Japan course full of water and tight boundaries.
entries.hltb_note: HLTB entry is NES-only (1 main completions logged; Wikidata-linked) - low sample

entries.title: Legacy of the Wizard
entries.summary: Nihon Falcom's Dragon Slayer IV, published in NA by Broderbund: the Drasle family, one member at a time, explores a vast labyrinth for four crowns that unlock the Dragon Slayer sword to kill the dragon Keela.
entries.why_it_matters: An early open-world, non-linear action RPG with Metroidvania-style design, and one of the few Dragon Slayer games released in the West.
entries.gameplay_notes: Father, mother, son, daughter and pet each have different strengths (the father hits hardest but can't jump high; the mother is the only one who can use certain magic items). Each of the five sections is built around one character. Return home to switch characters and get passwords.

entries.title: The Legend of Kage
entries.summary: Taito's NES version of its 1985 arcade ninja game: Kage fights through forest, secret passage, fortress wall and castle to rescue Princess Kiri.
entries.gameplay_notes: Kodachi sword and unlimited shuriken, with huge leaps. Crystal balls upgrade Kage's clothes for bigger shuriken or more speed, and a hit in upgraded clothes reverts them instead of killing you. The NES version requires three rescues, with the seasons changing each loop.
entries.hltb_note: HLTB NES platform row (17 completions logged; Wikidata-linked)

entries.title: The Legend of Zelda
entries.summary: Nintendo's 1986 action-adventure, released on NES cartridge in 1987: Link explores Hyrule to recover the eight fragments of the Triforce of Wisdom and rescue Princess Zelda from Ganon.
entries.why_it_matters: Designed by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka; one of the most influential games ever made and a 6.5-million seller. Among the first cartridges with a save battery.
entries.gameplay_notes: Open overhead world. Find caves with a sword, shops and secrets, and nine dungeons with items such as the boomerang and recorder. You can reach the final boss without ever taking the sword. Beating the game unlocks a harder Second Quest with new dungeons.
entries.hltb_note: HLTB NES platform row (712 completions logged; Wikidata-linked)
entries.collecting_notes: The NA box has a die-cut window showing the gold-coloured cartridge; Next Generation named it one of the five greatest game packages.
